## Instructions for Accurately Documenting Failed Building Fire-Safety Checks

These instructions detail the process for thoroughly documenting failures identified during building fire-safety checks. Accurate documentation is crucial for rectification, follow-up inspections, and legal/insurance purposes.

**1. Start with the Inspection Records.**

* **Identify the Original Inspection Report:** Locate the complete and original inspection report (physical or electronic) that initiated the follow-up/failure documentation. This serves as the baseline.
* **Review the Scope:** Re-familiarize yourself with the specific fire-safety areas covered in the original inspection.  This ensures you are addressing all related issues.
* **Note the Inspector & Date:** Clearly record the name of the original inspector and the date of the initial inspection in your documentation. This provides context.
* **Refer to Referenced Codes & Standards:**  The original report will likely reference specific fire codes, standards (NFPA, IBC,
